brief.headline: Offer to pay in 15 days (freeing ₹26.60 L cash for us) in return for a 12% price cut — their cash is stuck much longer than rivals and they borrow at 12.16%

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a 12% price cut if we pay them in 15 days instead of 30
priceAsk.target: 12% off current price — roughly their borrowing rate of 12.16%
priceAsk.basis: They borrow money at 12.16%, so paying them 15 days early is worth about that much to them. Our current price sits at the top of the market-fair band (₹205–305/kg, typical ₹250/kg), so there's room to move down and still stay fair.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Propose paying in 15 days (instead of current 30 days) in exchange for the price cut
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: ₹26.60 L cash freed up for us

brief.financialLeverage: They keep only 2.3% of every ₹100 they sell, so margins are razor-thin. But their cash is stuck for 101d — much longer than similar firms (64d) — and they borrow at 12.16%, so faster payment is valuable to them. We're only 0.61% of their ₹1064.86 Cr revenue, so we're a tiny customer and can't squeeze hard. Their credit rating is middling (CARE BBB+ / Stable), they owe 1.25× their own cash, and they've had EPF payment delays — all signs cash is tight. The smart play: offer to help their cash crunch with faster payment, but tie it to a price cut sized to their borrowing cost.

evidence.point: Their cash is stuck for 101 days, much longer than rivals at 64 days
We're a tiny 0.61% of their ₹1064.86 Cr revenue
They owe 1.25 times their own cash
They keep only 2.3% profit on sales
Credit rating is middling and they've had EPF payment delays
evidence.figure: CARE BBB+ / Stable; EPF payment delays

alternates.name: Huhtamaki India Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexible-packaging converter already supplying FDC in small volumes — proven and scalable for laminate sachets (₹2755.75 Cr revenue, health C 58/100)

alternates.name: UFLEX Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexibles giant doing both film and conversion — can second-source at big scale (₹17547.92 Cr revenue, health C 48/100)

alternates.name: Constantia Parikh Packaging Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Global group's India arm for pharma blister and sachet laminates — strong second source (₹222.04 Cr revenue, health D 31/100)

risks: They're in the grey zone financially (Altman Z 2.36) and have delayed EPF payments — don't push so hard you tip a fragile supplier over; keep the tone collaborative.
Margins are paper-thin (2.3%) — a steep price cut with no payment-speed trade could hurt supply; always tie the cut to faster pay.
We're only 0.61% of their business, so we have little clout — lead with the mutual benefit (we help their cash, they help our price), not demands.
Credit rating is CARE BBB+ / Stable and debt is 1.25× equity — watch supply continuity; consider qualifying a second source in parallel.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to help your cash flow by paying you in fifteen days instead of thirty — in return, we're looking for a twelve percent price reduction that reflects the value of that faster cash to you.
